_comment: Routes AA actually buys, for the Spend Guard shadow evaluation. Generated from the repository at the commit below; every description carries its source. Where no provider description exists, `description` is the verbatim `name` field and description_source.kind is name_only - nothing here is invented. The integration spec 3-5 that names this file was not available to the author, so this shape is a proposal; rename or reshape it to match the spec.

A.purpose: Produce one daily call - buy or skip, with direction and a size proposal - for the ERC-8004 agent, by scoring three signals into a bounded score and comparing it against a threshold.
required_data: strength signal: Nansen net flow in USD for the token
conviction signal: Hyperliquid open-interest positioning skew
direction signal: whale intent with a confidence

B.purpose: Daily briefing: fetch every configured Mode B endpoint and log the result.
B.required_data_note: Mode B enumerates NO per-route need. It iterates the whole endpoint array and buys all 14 unconditionally, so there is nothing in the code saying what any single route is required to supply. Left empty rather than invented.

C.purpose: Weekly report: fetch every configured Mode C endpoint and log the result.
C.required_data_note: As Mode B: all 5 are bought unconditionally, with no per-route need stated.

_task_origin_legend.code: Derived from the agent's own code, with citations. Only Mode A's three signals qualify.
_task_origin_legend.demo: Written for the demo harness. Not a claim about what the agent actually needs; the agent declares no per-route need for these.

demo._comment: Demo-only switches. All default to false. They exist so a live run can be made to show a specific Spend Guard verdict on a real x402 settlement; none of them changes what the agent buys when they are off.

duplicate_purchase._why_this_route: Cheapest route on Base at USD 0.05, GET, no request body, and the agent's own README records that it returns zero candidates anyway (README.md:31) - so the wasted second purchase is as small and as harmless as the endpoint list allows.
duplicate_purchase._what_it_does: Requests this one route a second time in the same run. The second candidate carries the first purchase in prior_acquisitions, which is what makes the deterministic check fire.
duplicate_purchase._expected_verdict: First purchase PAY. Second: deterministic signal EXACT_REPURCHASE, aggregated to HOLD by rule 3.
duplicate_purchase._shadow_mode_caveat: Shadow mode does not block. The second payment still settles on chain; the ledger records that the guard would have held it. That contrast is the demo.
